questions.prompt: A lift moves upwards at a constant speed. How does the upward tension compare with its weight?
questions.explain: Constant velocity means balanced forces (first law).

questions.prompt: A 0.5 kg ball is kicked with a resultant force of 150 N. What is its acceleration?
A 60 kg skater at 4 m/s catches a 20 kg bag that was at rest. What is their combined velocity?
Why do you jerk backwards when a stationary bus suddenly starts?
options: Your body tends to stay at rest (inertia)
questions.explain: The bus moves forward under you while your body tends to stay where it was.

questions.prompt: A 1 kg and a 5 kg stone are dropped from the same height in a vacuum. Which statement is correct?
options: They land at the same time
questions.explain: All objects have the same acceleration g in free fall.

questions.prompt: A car of mass 1000 kg slows from 20 m/s to 0 in 4 s. What is the average braking force?
questions.explain: Change in momentum = 1000 × 20 = 20 000 kg m/s; F = 20 000 ÷ 4 = 5000 N (or a = 5 m/s², F = ma).

questions.prompt: A horse pulls a cart. By the third law, the cart pulls back on the horse with an equal force. So how can they move?
options: They can’t move: the forces cancel
The horse pulls first, before the cart reacts
The horse pushes back on the ground, and the ground pushes the horse forward more than the cart pulls back
The forces are not really equal
questions.explain: Only forces on the same object matter for its motion. On the horse: the ground’s forward push is bigger than the cart’s backward pull.

questions.prompt: Use two of Newton’s laws to explain why wearing a helmet reduces head injuries in a two-wheeler accident.
questions.modelAnswer: First law: in a crash the rider’s head keeps moving (inertia) until something stops it. The helmet’s foam crushes, making the stopping time longer. Since force = change in momentum ÷ time (second law), a longer time means a smaller force on the head, reducing injury. The hard shell also spreads the force over a bigger area.
rubric: Smaller force from F = change in momentum ÷ time
questions.explain: Criterion D: applying physics to safety.
